chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions (I think it was Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal or Ali ibn al-Hakam), from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who divorces his wife, when does she become irrevocably divorced from him? He said: When the blood emerges from the third menstruation, she controls herself. I said: So is it for her that she may marry in that state? He said: Yes, but she does not give herself over [to her husband] until she has purified from the blood.
ai.seo_question: When does a woman become irrevocably divorced after her husband divorces her three times?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment of irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in) by linking it to the emergence of blood from the third menstruation, a key indicator in Shia jurisprudence. While the woman gains autonomy to remarry at this point, the text specifies she must complete her purification (taharah) from that specific blood flow before the marriage contract can be finalized, reflecting the interplay between physical purity and legal status.
